title: An isometric field isomorphism extends to concrete subfield closures
statement: Let $H$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued absolute value, meaning $|x|\geq0$, $|x|=0\iff x=0$, $|1|=1$, $|xy|=|x||y|$, and $|x+y|\leq |x|+|y|$. Assume that $H$ is complete for $d(x,y)=|x-y|$. Let $F,G\subseteq H$ be subfields, equipped with the restricted absolute value, and let $f:F\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ be a field isomorphism satisfying $|f(x)|=|x|$ for all $x\in F$. Write $\overline F,\overline G$ for their metric closures inside $H$. These closures are subfields, and there exists a unique field isomorphism $\overline f:\overline F\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline G$ extending $f$ and satisfying $|\overline f(x)|=|x|$ for every $x\in\overline F$. In particular $d(\overline f(x),\overline f(y))=d(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in\overline F$.

source.place: Isometry.completion_extension, lines 193–197; Isometry.extensionHom and extensionHom_coe, lines 209–214. Concrete-closure reformulation additionally requires identifying the completion image with the closure; that argument is agent-written.

proof.text: The absolute value gives a metric topological field: addition is continuous by $|(x+y)-(x'+y')|\leq|x-x'|+|y-y'|$, negation is an isometry, and multiplication is continuous by $|xy-x'y'|\leq |x|\,|y-y'|+|y'|\,|x-x'|$ (near a fixed point $|y'|\leq |y|+1$). Away from zero, $|x^{-1}-y^{-1}|=|x-y|/(|x||y|)$ and $|y-x|<|x|/2$ implies $|y|>|x|/2$, so inversion is continuous there. Apply [lem-trf-subfield-topological-closure] to obtain subfields $\overline F,\overline G$, closed in $H$ and containing $F,G$. The inclusions $F\to\overline F$ and $G\to\overline G$ preserve distance and have dense image: a ball about a point of a closure meets the original set, by the definition of closure. Use throughout the restricted metrics and field operations.

source.place: IsDenseInducing.extendRingHom, lines 274–293; agent assembly for concrete closures using Field.lean:60–74 and DenseEmbedding.lean:359–384.

proof.text: For $a,b\in F$, $|f(a)-f(b)|=|f(a-b)|=|a-b|$. Thus $f:F\to H$ is uniformly continuous (take $\delta=\epsilon$); $f^{-1}:G\to H$ is likewise an isometry because every pair in $G$ has preimages in $F$. Apply [lem-trf-dense-isometric-ring-hom-extension] with $(A,B,C)=(F,\overline F,H)$, $i$ the inclusion, and $h=f$. It gives a uniformly continuous ring homomorphism $T:\overline F\to H$ extending $f$. Apply it again with $(G,\overline G,H)$ and $f^{-1}$ to obtain a uniformly continuous ring homomorphism $S:\overline G\to H$ extending $f^{-1}$. Completeness is needed only for the codomain $H$, which is complete by hypothesis.

source.place: IsDenseInducing.extendRingHom, lines 274–293; agent assembly for concrete closures using Field.lean:60–74 and DenseEmbedding.lean:359–384.

proof.text: The set $T^{-1}(\overline G)$ is closed in $\overline F$, since $T$ is continuous and $\overline G$ is closed; it contains $F$ because $T(a)=f(a)\in G$. The closed-predicate clause of [lem-trf-dense-closed-predicate] gives $T(\overline F)\subseteq\overline G$. Similarly $S(\overline G)\subseteq\overline F$. Hence corestrict to continuous ring homomorphisms $t:\overline F\to\overline G$ and $s:\overline G\to\overline F$. Corestriction preserves continuity because inverse images of relatively open sets are inverse images of ambient opens.

source.place: IsDenseInducing.extendRingHom, lines 274–293; agent assembly for concrete closures using Field.lean:60–74 and DenseEmbedding.lean:359–384.

proof.text: For each $a\in F$, the continuous real-valued functions $y\mapsto d(t(a),t(y))$ and $y\mapsto d(a,y)$ on $\overline F$ agree on $F$ by the isometry of $f$; [lem-trf-dense-closed-predicate] makes them equal everywhere. Now fix any $y\in\overline F$ and apply the same equality clause in the variable $x$ to $x\mapsto d(t(x),t(y))$ and $x\mapsto d(x,y)$, whose equality on $F$ was just proved. Thus $d(t(x),t(y))=d(x,y)$ for all $x,y$. Continuity of these distance functions follows directly from $|d(u,v)-d(u',v')|\leq d(u,u')+d(v,v')$. Since the ring map sends $0$ to $0$, taking $y=0$ gives $|t(x)|=|x|$.

source.place: IsDenseInducing.extendRingHom, lines 274–293; agent assembly for concrete closures using Field.lean:60–74 and DenseEmbedding.lean:359–384.

proof.text: The continuous maps $s\circ t$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\overline F}$ agree on $F$, since $S(f(a))=f^{-1}(f(a))=a$. By [lem-trf-dense-closed-predicate] they agree on $\overline F$. Similarly $t\circ s=\operatorname{id}_{\overline G}$. Therefore $t$ is a field isomorphism, with inverse $s$, extending $f$. Any other absolute-value-preserving field isomorphism $r:\overline F\to\overline G$ extending $f$ satisfies $d(r(x),r(y))=|r(x-y)|=|x-y|$ and is continuous. Since $r$ and $t$ agree on dense $F$, the same equality clause gives $r=t$.
